title: Heated vessel control with a PID loop
summary: Tune a PID controller on a real heated vessel: remove the offset of a P-only loop, ride out a door-open disturbance and switch between manual and automatic without a bump.
objectives: Read SP, PV and MV in a trend and recognise the offset of a P-only loop
Remove the offset with integral action and keep the overshoot small
Use output limits, manual mode and bumpless transfer of the PID block
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    AutoMode : BOOL; (* Selector S1 in position AUTO. *)
    TempRaw : INT; (* Temperature transmitter TT-1: 0..10000 = 0..150 degC. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    HeaterRaw : INT; (* Heater power controller: 0..10000 = 0..100 %. *)
    HeaterLamp : BOOL; (* Lamp H1: the heater is on. *)
    AlarmLamp : BOOL; (* Lamp H2: overtemperature. *)
    Temperature : REAL; (* Vessel temperature in degC. *)
END_VAR
VAR
    Setpoint : REAL := 60.0; (* degC *)
    Kp : REAL := 4.0; (* proportional gain, % per degC *)
    Ti : TIME := T#0s; (* integral time; T#0s = no integral action *)
    Td : TIME := T#0s; (* derivative time *)
    PowerMin : REAL := 0.0; (* output limits, % *)
    PowerMax : REAL := 100.0;
    ManualPower : REAL := 20.0; (* heater power in MAN, % *)
    Power : REAL; (* controller output, % *)
    Loop : PID;
END_VAR

Temperature := INT_TO_REAL(TempRaw) * 0.015;

(* The loop runs with P only and has no MAN mode yet. Tune it in the Tuning tab,
   then complete it: see the instructions. *)
Loop(SP := Setpoint, PV := Temperature, KP := Kp, TI := Ti, TD := Td,
     MV_MIN := PowerMin, MV_MAX := PowerMax, MV => Power);

HeaterRaw := REAL_TO_INT(Power * 100.0);
HeaterLamp := Power > 0.5;
AlarmLamp := Temperature > 90.0;
END_PROGRAM
instructions: Build & Load the starter and open the Tuning tab. The loop runs with P only: the temperature settles below the 60 °C setpoint. Watch SP, PV and MV in the trend.
Add integral action: change TI in the Tuning tab until the temperature settles at 60 °C and never exceeds 65 °C, then write that value into the program as the initial value of Ti.
Open the vessel door in the Tuning tab. The heat loss is a disturbance; the controller must bring the temperature back to 60 °C while the door stays open.
Wire the MAN/AUTO selector S1: MANUAL := NOT AutoMode and MV_MAN := ManualPower. In MAN the heater runs at 20 %; switching to AUTO must not make the output jump.
Keep the output within 0..100 % with MV_MIN and MV_MAX and scale it to HeaterRaw (0..10000).
hints: With P only the heater needs an error to work, so the temperature stays below the setpoint. The integral part grows while there is an error and removes that offset.
A TI of about 20 s suits this vessel. A much shorter TI makes the temperature overshoot and swing.
Let the PID block switch between MAN and AUTO: give it MANUAL and MV_MAN instead of choosing Power with an IF. Its integral follows the manual output, so the transfer is bumpless.

criteria.title: Temperature shows the vessel temperature
criteria.onFail: Temperature was not about 20 °C in the cold vessel. Scale TempRaw: 0..10000 is 0..150 °C.

criteria.title: The vessel reaches the setpoint
criteria.onFail: The vessel did not reach 58 °C within 120 s. A P-only loop stays below the setpoint: add integral action (TI).

criteria.title: The temperature settles at 60 °C without offset
criteria.onFail: From 150 s on the temperature left 58.5..61.5 °C. Remove the offset with TI and avoid a swinging loop.

criteria.title: The temperature never exceeds 65 °C
criteria.onFail: The temperature overshot above 65 °C. Use a longer TI or a smaller KP.

criteria.title: The loop compensates the open door
criteria.onFail: With the door open since 180 s the temperature was not back within 58.5..61.5 °C by 330 s. Only integral action can compensate a lasting heat loss.

criteria.title: In MAN the heater runs at 20 %
criteria.onFail: In MAN HeaterRaw was not about 2000 (20 %). Give the block MANUAL := NOT AutoMode and MV_MAN := ManualPower.

criteria.title: Switching from MAN to AUTO does not make the output jump
criteria.onFail: 0.5 s after switching to AUTO HeaterRaw was outside 1500..3000: the output jumped. Let the PID block switch with MANUAL and MV_MAN.

criteria.title: The PLC runs without a fault
criteria.onFail: The PLC stopped with a runtime fault, for example inverted output limits.
